limitations: The close event is declared as a creation event and is observed before the close call; the property does not condition monitoring on normal return from close().
The rule does not inspect whether IOException was thrown, caught, suppressed, or absent.
The rule does not test thread identity, locking, happens-before relationships, or synchronization.
The supplied property source does not specify report cardinality for repeated manipulate calls after a match; generated-monitor/runtime behavior would be required to establish that.
Only call join points covered by the actual weaving/instrumentation configuration can be observed.
predicates: manipulate: `(call(* Reader+.read(..)) || call(* Reader+.ready(..)) || call(* Reader+.mark(..)) || call(* Reader+.reset(..)) || call(* Reader+.skip(..))) && target(r)`
Both pointcuts use before advice, so each event is recorded at the call join point before the callee executes.
`Reader+` is an AspectJ subtype pattern and includes `java.io.Reader` and its subtypes; `target(r)` is a runtime target-instance predicate.
detector_semantics.claim: The rule emits its critical message upon a match of the declared extended regular expression `close+ manipulate+` for monitor parameter `r`; its message describes this as invocation of a selected Reader operation after `close()`.

unknowns: The supplied rule does not state whether the generated monitor reports every post-close manipulate event, only a first match, or some other report cardinality.
The rule source alone does not identify the actual agent/weaver configuration, excluded packages, class-loader coverage, or whether all candidate call sites were instrumented.
The rule source does not define cross-thread ordering beyond the runtime order in which its before-call events are observed.
The rule does not establish whether the concrete Reader implementation's close() completed, whether it was idempotent in practice, or whether a later operation actually threw IOException.
The property source does not state how the monitor handles object identity/lifecycle after garbage collection or monitor eviction; that requires generated-monitor/runtime implementation evidence.

documented_behavior: `java.io.Reader` is the abstract API for character streams.
`Reader.close()` closes the stream and releases associated system resources.
Once a Reader stream has been closed, subsequent `read()`, `ready()`, `mark()`, `reset()`, and `skip()` invocations throw `IOException`.
The governed operation groups read characters, test readiness, establish a mark, reset position, and skip characters.
preconditions: The documented post-close `IOException` statement applies after the stream has been closed, whereas this detector records entry to `close()` before that call completes.
`mark()` and `reset()` may independently throw `IOException` when the operation is unsupported, no valid mark exists, or another I/O error occurs.
`skip(long)` may independently throw `IllegalArgumentException` for a negative count, in addition to `IOException` for an I/O error.
unknowns: Whether a specific concrete subtype's `close()` invocation completed normally in the observed execution.
Whether a concrete subtype has nonstandard behavior despite the Reader API contract.
Whether concurrent close and manipulate calls had a synchronization relationship that establishes a completed closed state before the manipulate call.

events.condition: Observed before a call matching `call(* Reader+.close(..))` when its runtime target is bound as `r`, an instance of `java.io.Reader` or a subtype. The rule tests no return value, exception, completion status, argument value, or implementation-specific closed-state field.
events.name: close

events.condition: Observed before a call matching one of `call(* Reader+.read(..))`, `call(* Reader+.ready(..))`, `call(* Reader+.mark(..))`, `call(* Reader+.reset(..))`, or `call(* Reader+.skip(..))`, when its runtime target is bound as `r`, an instance of `java.io.Reader` or a subtype. The rule matches all argument lists for each named method; a source substring alone is insufficient without resolving the call and target type.
events.name: manipulate

important_note: This is a temporal before-call monitor, not proof that `close()` completed successfully, that the object was actually in a closed implementation state, or that the later call threw `IOException`. Both selected events are observed before their invoked methods execute.
forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: That a reported `close()` invocation returned normally or released resources.
That the later `read`, `ready`, `mark`, `reset`, or `skip` invocation actually executed, completed, or threw `IOException`.
That the concrete Reader subtype conforms to the documented `java.io.Reader` post-close contract.
That methods not named by the rule, including `markSupported()`, `transferTo()`, `readAllAsString()`, or `readAllLines()`, are covered.
That the finding establishes a security vulnerability, exploit path, confidentiality impact, integrity impact, availability impact, or attacker control.
That a lexical occurrence such as `read(` denotes a governed call without resolved method/target-type and runtime-target evidence.
That the reported application class or method is itself the API governed by the specification; the governed API is `java.io.Reader` and its subtypes.

security_semantics.runtime_claim: The documented Reader contract says that the selected operations throw `IOException` once the stream has been closed, but this rule does not observe the closed-state transition or the later call's outcome.
security_semantics.detector_claim: The detector claims a temporal API-protocol match: a selected Reader operation was invoked after an observed `close` call on the same target.

compatibility: The runtime must use pointcut/weaving semantics compatible with the supplied JavaMOP/AspectJ-style `call`, `target`, and `Reader+` clauses.
Instrumentation coverage must include the relevant call sites and class-loading paths.
For subtype scope, confirm the concrete runtime receiver is assignable to `java.io.Reader`; AspectJ `+` subtype matching includes the base type and subtypes.
runtime: A runtime trace or monitor record showing a before-call `close` event followed by a before-call `manipulate` event with the same bound target object.

If claiming an actual post-closure API violation rather than a detector match, evidence that `close` completed and that the later governed invocation occurred afterward under the relevant concurrency ordering.
If claiming the documented exception behavior occurred, the exception outcome from the manipulate call.
source_level: Resolve the receiver and invoked declaration to `java.io.Reader` or a subtype and to one of `close`, `read`, `ready`, `mark`, `reset`, or `skip`; method-name text by itself is not sufficient.
Establish that the two calls concern the same object identity, not merely variables with the same name or type.
For a source-level interpretation of “after close,” inspect control flow and exception paths around `close()`, including whether the call can throw before resource closure.

name: Reader_ManipulateAfterClose
semantic_scope: For every finding of this rule, the detector observes a before-call event for `close(..)` and then a before-call event for `read(..)`, `ready(..)`, `mark(..)`, `reset(..)`, or `skip(..)` on the same runtime target object bound as `r`. `Reader+` includes `java.io.Reader` and its subtypes, and `target(r)` requires that target object to be an instance of the bound type.
known_false_positive_shapes: `close()` is entered and throws before it successfully closes the underlying stream, but a later governed call is still reported because the monitor recorded close before execution.

One thread enters `close()`, while another thread enters a governed operation before `close()` has completed; the monitor's before-call ordering can report the operation even though completed-closure ordering is not established.
A concrete implementation has unusual or nonconforming lifecycle behavior, including reopening or delegating lifecycle state in a way not represented by the monitor's event history.
The application deliberately invokes a governed method after close solely to obtain and handle the documented `IOException`; the rule still reports the protocol event sequence.
A later call is intercepted before execution but does not reach normal method execution because of another runtime failure or dispatch-related issue.
protocol: For the same bound runtime target object `r`: `close(r)+ manipulate(r)+`, where `manipulate` is a call to `read`, `ready`, `mark`, `reset`, or `skip`.

detector_examples.message: Reader_ManipulateAfterClose read(), ready(), mark(), reset() or skip() was invoked after close().
